questions.q: What does an upsert do when a CSV row matches an existing record on the chosen ID field?
options: It inserts a duplicate record
It deletes the existing record
It updates that record
It skips the row silently
questions.explain: A match means update; no match means insert.

questions.q: What does an upsert do when a CSV row has no match?
options: It inserts a new record
It fails every row in the file
It updates the first record it finds
It moves the row to the Recycle Bin
questions.explain: Rows without a match are inserted as new records.

questions.q: What is an External ID field?
options: A field Salesforce adds to every object to track deletions
A permission that lets external users log in
The 18-character Id Salesforce generates
A custom field marked as External ID that stores a key from another system
questions.explain: External ID fields let you match Salesforce records to keys from an outside system.

questions.q: Why is upsert a good fit for repeatable loads?
options: It bypasses validation rules
Re-running the same file updates existing rows instead of creating duplicates, and you need no Salesforce Ids
It runs faster than every other operation by skipping matching
It automatically schedules itself
questions.explain: Matching on your own key means the same load can run again safely.

questions.q: What happens when an upsert row matches more than one existing record?
options: All matching records are updated
The oldest record wins automatically
That row errors, so the matching field should be unique and reliable
Salesforce merges the matches into one
questions.explain: An ambiguous match can't be resolved, so it produces an error for that row.
